description: R08 MediaResourceTests checkpoint: safe Rust owns media-resource state, layered origin/base-path propagation, profile/action/menu traversal, emoji handling, icon fallback, bell-sound replacement and fragment appearance behavior. Eighteen contracts are Exact; the four real-resolver contracts are Partial only for their Win32 filesystem, environment, wallpaper and package-context adapter.

entries.notes: Rust visits the eleven inbox media resources once with InBox origin and preserves resolved profile icon/background values.
Layering reproduces the native 10 inbox, one ProfilesDefaults and one User resolver observations plus the effective default/user profile icons.
Fragment profile/action resources retain Fragment origin and the fragment base path while materializing resolved runtime values.
Recursive new-tab-menu traversal finds all six user icons in profile/action/folder entries without changing the eleven inbox observations.
Resolved resources are skipped on later passes; a runtime profile-icon replacement is pending until one User-origin resolver visit completes it.
The five Microsoft symbol/emoji icon vectors resolve to themselves without invoking the external media resolver.
A rejected icon inherited from profiles.defaults falls back to the command line owned by the defaults source.
A rejected profile-owned icon falls back to that profile's explicit command line.
A rejected profile-owned icon with no command-line override falls back to the default cmd.exe command line.
An inherited rejected icon keeps its source fallback instead of adopting a child profile command line.
An inherited rejected icon with no child command-line setting falls back to cmd.exe.
An explicit null profile icon bypasses media resolution and falls back to the profile's explicit command line.
An explicit null icon without a profile command-line override falls back to cmd.exe.
A user bellSound array replaces the inherited two-item list and retains the rejected state of its sole resource.
A fragment updates an existing profile icon by GUID and resolves it against the fragment base path.
A fragment action icon is retained in the runtime action map and resolved with the fragment base path.
disabledProfileSources suppresses fragment media traversal while preserving the inbox profile icon.
User replacement of an unfocused appearance re-parents missing media fields to the focused appearance while user-owned fields retain the user base path and shared resources retain identity.

Rust owns Windows-style absolute/relative traversal, slash normalization, environment expansion flow and candidate validation. Actual file existence and environment lookup are supplied by MediaPlatform rather than Win32.
The none and desktopWallpaper decisions are owned in Rust; desktop-wallpaper discovery itself remains a MediaPlatform operation.
Rust owns file/HTTPS/ms-resource/ms-appx and rejected-scheme decisions plus local leaf fallback; filesystem existence and packaged-app context remain platform responsibilities.
Rust preserves UNC and Win32 namespace candidates and the native acceptance decision is exercised through MediaPlatform; real share/local-path existence remains platform-bound.
